newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico continues natgas promotion with rights sale.
newsitem.headline: Mexico continues natgas promotion with rights sale.

text.p: Mexico granted its second concession for private natural gas distribution on Wednesday as part of efforts to promote more wide-spread use of the fuel.

A consortium of U.S. companies Enova International, Pacific Enterprises International and Mexican Proxima Gas won 30-year rights to distribute natural gas in the northern Mexico state of Chihuahua after proposing the lowest cost to consumers of $1.30 per gigacalorie in the next 5 years.
"We are actively engaged in a marketing effort to promote the safety features and economic benefits," Pacific Enterprises vice president John Peterson told a news conference.

If the winning bidder fails to service the number of clients it promised in its proposal after five years, it is slapped with a $10 million penalty, Energy Regulatory Commission president Hector Olea said.

Unlike the first natural gas concession, also won by DGN last August in the border city of Mexicali, Baja California state, the Chihuahua zone already has natural gas service, provided by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).

The consortium will pay $3.1 million for the transfer of Pemex's distribution assets, a 27.7 kilometer pipeline. Although DGN has won both of Mexico's concessions to date to distribute natural gas, Peterson said the company has no intention of creating a monopoly and plans to bid for about half of the 10 other concessions to be auctioned this year.

The Mexico government does not prevent any one company or consortium from winning all of the concessions, Olea added. The Federal Competition Commission would investigate any monopoly concerns, he added.
Natural gas consumption in the area is expected to grow by about 18.6 billion cubic feet per year, 14.5 billion in the industrial sector and 3.2 billion residentially.
In Mexicali, the group said it would charge $1.14 per gigacalorie for a minimum coverage of 25,346 clients and an investment of $25 million.

Proxima Gas is composed of investors from Baja California state. Enova distributes natural gas in southern California and has more than a million customers in the United States. Pacific Enterprises distributes, transports and stores natural gas along the west coast.
The winning companies participated equally in the bid under the name Distribuidora de Gas Natural de Mexicali (DGN).
Other bidders for the Chihuahua region included Spain's Repsol with Gas Natural de Latinoamerica and U.S. NorAm Energy and Mexican private construction company Corporacion Gutsa.

Mexico's government is currently accepting bids for natural gas distribution in regions encompassing Hermosillo, Sonora state and Toluca, Mexico state. Other regions scheduled for auction later in the year include Mexico City, Tampico, Tamaulipas state and Cuernavaca, Morelos state.
